minutes.headline: Committee adopted its mission, core values and FY18 goals, and heard the draft FY19 capital plan.
minutes.summary: The facilities director presented the draft ten-year capital plan, centred on Turkey Hill's 50th year, asbestos abatement and air conditioning, and the committee asked for the shade structure timing to be rebalanced. The committee then adopted the mission, vision and core values, the superintendent's goals and its own goals. A member was appointed to the new Athletic Advisory, and the Charter appointments were put off to the next meeting.

what_happened.line: The School Committee adopted its mission, vision and core values; the minutes do not record how members voted.
The committee approved the superintendent's FY18 goals and its own FY18 goals; the vote counts were not audible.
The facilities director presented the draft ten-year capital plan and will revise it, mainly the shade structure timing, for an action item at the next meeting.
The Turkey Hill asbestos abatement project is on budget but has little contingency, and a liquidated damages clause applies if the contractor misses the deadline.
A member was appointed to the Athletic Advisory, and the Charter appointments were postponed to the next meeting.

why_it_matters: The capital plan sets the schedule for building work such as asbestos abatement, classroom air conditioning, boilers and roofs, which compete for the same limited capital funds and can reach the town budget, mostly taxes.
A thin contingency on the Turkey Hill abatement means a cost overrun or delay would need to be covered from another source.
watch_next: A revised capital plan, with shade structure timing changed, returns as an action item at the committee's next meeting.
The postponed Charter appointments are due at the next meeting.
